newsitem.title: JAPAN: Seven Japanese brokers see losses in first half.
newsitem.headline: Seven Japanese brokers see losses in first half.

text.p: Seven second-tier Japanese brokerages said on Thursday they would post losses in the first half of the current business year, hurt by lower-than-expected stock turnover and falling market share.

The country's biggest securities house, Nomura Securities Co Ltd, also said separately that it would post net losses in the six months to September 30 as it provides financial support to a non-bank affiliate.

The parent current losses at the seven firms are expected to range from Dai-Ichi Securities' 800 million yen ($7.33 million) to Kankaku Securities' 4.1 billion yen ($37.6 million) for the first six months. The other five firms are New Japan Securities, Wako Securities, Yamatane Securities, Cosmo Securities and Tokyo Securities

Company executives said that while the average daily turnover on the Tokyo Stock Exchange in the first five months was relatively good, that did not help the balance sheet of the second-tier brokers as their mainstay retail clients were reluctant to pour money into stocks.

An executive at Yamatane told reporters: "The market activity so far this year has mainly come from foreigners and institutional investors, and this did not help boost our income as our company's main customers are small investors."
Average daily turnover on the Tokyo exchange was 430.5 billion yen ($3.94 billion) in the first five months of 1996/97, against 374 billion yen ($3.43 billion) in the previous business year.

An executive at Sanyo Securities said the company had originally forecast average turnover of 450 billion yen ($4.12 billion) this year, but had revised it to 400 billion yen ($3.66 billion) for the first half and 360 billion yen ($3.30 billion) for the second.
Two other second-tier brokers, Okasan Securities and Sanyo Securities, said they would post parent current profits for the first six months, but much lower than they earlier forecast.
For the full year, eight of the 10 second-tier brokers expect profits. Yamatane and Kankaku expect to post losses. Kokusai Securities did not give a new forecast.

An analyst said it had become difficult for many second-tier brokers to trade stocks and bonds actively due to a long slump in the stock market, which improved only recently. Expectations that interest rates would rise also made it difficult for brokers to trade bonds actively as they did in the previous business year, he said.
Meanwhile, Nomura vice president Atsushi Saito told reporters it would provide 371 billion yen ($3.40 billion) to its non-bank affiliate Nomura Finance Co to help write off problem loans.
Nomura plans to post special losses of 371 billion yen ($3.40 billion) for the first half of 1996/97, which would probably result in a parent net loss for the period, he said.

Among Japan's "Big Four" securities firms, Nikko Securities revised downward its earnings forecast for the first half earlier this week. Another big broker, Yamaichi Securities, will also revise its earnings forecast down soon, analysts said. ($1=109 yen)
